newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends unchanged from previous close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends unchanged from previous close.

text.p: Hong Kong's gold market ended unchanged on Tuesday from New York's Monday close after a day of dull trade as some players licked their wounds following last week's price surge, gold dealers and traders said.
"We saw some light currency-related buying out of Japan," said one gold trader.
Others reported some buying out of Europe in the afternoon.
Bullion ended at US$367.90/368.40 an ounce against New York's US$367.90/368.30 close on Monday.
Some traders said the market was gripped by a holiday mood but others said gold's upside potential was seen limited, which kept buyers out of the market.
Credit Suisse bowing out of Hong Kong's bullion market would not have a significant impact, industry sources said.
"It's just one less competitor for thinning business," said a chief bullion dealer at a local firm. But the firm would lose out on potential business from China, the dealer said.
Physical demand remained thin, and some traders said the short-term outlook for gold jewellery consumption was middling.
Tael gold was still trading at a strong premium to spot gold with the U.S. dollar equivalent at $369.00/369.50 per ounce.
"The premium of tael gold is not just established by heavy physical buying," said one senior gold trader.
Tael gold's premium was also a result of an illiquid market, interest rates on the exchange and small traded volumes, he said.
Local gold ended HK$4 lower at HK$3,401 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -5.20 from its previous fix at +3.00
